R7BI-bear-backcountry-0003.name: 4.8 km W of Rogers Lakes
R7BI-bear-backcountry-0003.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R7BI-bear-backcountry-0003.parkWhat: pull off on West Lake Spur FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Burn from 2022 (fire G90789), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
W facing slope, 11 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland 90 m SW: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Northern Rockies Regional Municipality, about 255 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 59.88849, -126.51128, pull off on West Lake Spur FSR (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 11 km SW, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 576 m, about 276 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 140 m NW of the spot at 825 m (59.83831, -126.6788). Water: unnamed wetland 30 m SW (estimate).

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-53, Region 7B. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2024-10-05, closures 2026-10-16.
R7BI-bear-backcountry-0003.recDirections: Drive north from the Liard River Hot Springs Provincial Park about 20 minutes along the Alaska Hwy. Turn right on to the Smith River Forest Service Road. Continue to the end of the FSR at km 47. NOTE: This route is not intended for large rcreational vehciles.
R7BI-bear-backcountry-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 7-53: about 22 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.00 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: more than 5 km from a drivable road. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
